title: The Last Marker
concept: A solo motorcycle racer crosses the Baja California desert in 1967. His 1965 Triumph is failing. He is lost. He finds a trail marker left by a rider who came before him. The marker points two ways. He has to choose: water, or the course. Three minutes. Almost no dialogue.
tone: Sparse, tense, and sun-bleached. A Sergio Leone spaghetti western played as a quiet desert survival story.

visual_style.description: Locked 2.39:1 widescreen. Extreme wide shots cut against extreme close-ups. Long tense holds, then sharp cuts. Mostly a still camera, with slow push-ins. Warm sun-bleached 1960s film look, with grain. Charcoal blacks, bone whites, and a day that moves from amber to bronze to rose to blue dusk.

sound_design.description: The Triumph's single-cylinder engine is the lead sound. When it dies, the desert goes quiet: wind, sand, and cooling metal. One Spanish line, almost lost under the engine.
sound_design.music_approach: A score in the spirit of Ennio Morricone. Do not copy any melody.

characters.name: Miguel Vega
characters.description: 30. Mexican. Lean. Sun-darkened skin, deep lines around the eyes from years of squinting into wind and light. Short dark hair. Strong jaw. The wear is from sun and wind, not from age. He wears a white cotton shirt, a sun-bleached brown leather vest, khaki pants, and boots that have been resoled twice. Goggles sit on his forehead when he is not riding. No helmet. He is a ranch hand from outside Tecate. He races because the desert is the only place big enough for the thing inside him that has no name.

props.name: Breitling Top Time
props.description: Black reverse panda dial, stainless case, worn brown leather rally strap. He won it in a card game from a crop duster pilot in Mexicali. Locked on the left wrist.

vehicles.name: 1965 Triumph TR6SC
vehicles.description: Desert-modified 1965 Triumph TR6SC Trophy. Knobby tires, stripped fairing, pale dust. The film is set in 1967. The bike stays a 1965. Exhaust is locked on the right side.

test_objectives: One consistent rider across every shot.
A desert that feels like one place as the light changes.
A specific 1965 Triumph, including the engine and the kick.
The Breitling Top Time staying the same watch once the wrist is locked.
One barely audible line of Spanish.

setting.notes: Ron locked the year at 1967. The Triumph remains a 1965 model.

hero_props.name: 1965 Triumph TR6SC
hero_props.description: Desert-modified 1965 Triumph TR6SC. The film year is 1967. The bike year stays 1965. Exhaust is locked on the right side.

hero_props.name: Breitling Top Time
hero_props.description: Black reverse panda dial on a worn brown leather rally strap. Locked on the left wrist.

featured_product.target_audience: The buyer who would wear this watch.
featured_product.placement_intent: Subtle. The film is quietly about this watch: time running out, the race, and choosing water over finishing. The dial is legible only in a few story-driven close views.
rules: The dial is legible in a few key close-ups tied to time, the race, and water versus finishing.
Never make it ad-like. No logo-forward hero spins.
Do not add dialogue that names the brand. The script's one line does not name it.

decisions: The film cap is $500. Retakes count against the same cap.
The story is set in Baja California in 1967.

The reference look is a Sergio Leone spaghetti western: extreme wides against extreme close-ups, locked 2.39:1, long holds then sharp cuts, a warm grainy 1960s film look, and a mostly still camera with slow push-ins.
The score is in the spirit of Ennio Morricone. No melody is copied.
The hero props are the Triumph and the Breitling Top Time. Exhaust is locked on the right. The watch is locked on the left wrist.
